summary: Unexpected function-call ordering and duplicates when client circuit-breaker triggers SDK retries (Python & TS)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their client-side circuit-breaker trips during a multi-step orchestration that includes multiple tool/function calls, the Redwood SDK retries result in out-of-order tool invocations and occasional duplicate side-effects. Behavior is observed in both Python and TypeScript SDKs; symptoms are more frequent under load and when backoff jitter is disabled.

Impact:
- Several downstream orders processed twice (side-effects visible in customer's systems).
- Orchestration logic relies on sequential tool-call ordering; reordering breaks business invariants for a subset of requests (~0.6% of requests during incident window).
- Customer uses dedicated capacity and is in production in us-east-1.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-3 (customer-owned dedicated cluster)
- SDK versions: python-sdk v1.28.0, typescript-sdk v0.34.1
- Model: redwood/gpt-4o-mini-v1 + tool-runner-v2
- Network: customer behind a proxy that enforces 30s idle connection timeout

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided minimal repro):
1) Start an orchestration that issues three sequential tool calls: charge_customer(), provision_resource(), send_confirmation().
2) Configure client circuit-breaker to trip after 15s and to immediately trigger an SDK-level retry when the CB resets.
3) Simulate a transient router-side partial ACK (server accepted first two tool calls but connection dropped before final acknowledgement).
4) Observe server logs and customer system: sometimes provision_resource() runs twice; confirmation appears before provisioning in ~2% of repro runs.

Example client pseudocode (TypeScript):

const session = client.startSession({idempotencyScope: "orchestration-{{orderId}}"});
await session.callTool("charge_customer", {amount});
await session.callTool("provision_resource", {sku});
await session.callTool("send_confirmation", {email});

// client uses circuit-breaker library that retries entire session on error

Logs / Correlation IDs:
- Customer provided request IDs: rQf-20260310-xt9, rQf-20260310-xtA, rQf-20260311-bc1
- Partial server traces: https://kibana.redwood.internal/trace/rQf-20260310-xt9 (redacted)

Hypothesis:
- SDK-level automatic retry for session/resume combined with client circuit-breaker (which replays the entire session) results in re-sending previously-acked tool calls when the SDK treats ack windows as transient.
- Idempotency scope currently defaults to session-level for orchestration sessions; when the circuit-breaker replay causes a new session instance, idempotency keys are not being deduplicated at the per-action level, so side-effects may be replayed.
- Differences between Python and TS SDKs look to be about default retry/backoff configuration and whether the SDK re-uses the same per-action idempotency token on resume.

Immediate customer workaround suggested:
- Disable client circuit-breaker for orchestration that has external side-effects and rely on SDK retry/backoff only (if acceptable).
- Upgrade SDKs to the patched beta (see related PRs) that expose per-action idempotency tokens and make them opt-in.
- As short-term pattern: include explicit per-tool idempotency keys (action-level) rather than relying on session-scoped idempotency.

Requested by customer:
- Explanation of root cause and confirmation whether server dedup logic can be made more robust to session replays.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10: Initial triage by Support (Maya) — reproduced locally using customer's repro under a proxy with 30s idle timeout; observed behaviour consistent with report.

2026-03-11: SDK Engineers (Leo) ran additional tests:
- Python SDK v1.28.0 resumes session by reusing session-scoped idempotency header X-Idem-Scope but does NOT attach per-action ids by default.
- TS SDK v0.34.1 has a shorter default retry window and different backoff jitter. Under identical repro the TS run showed slightly fewer duplicates but still produced out-of-order confirmation events when CB replay occurred.

2026-03-11: SRE traced gateway logs: kernel shows that the first two tool calls return ACKs before TCP reset; the gateway marks session state as "in-flight" and later accepts a resumed session from a different connection; resumed session currently maps to same session id but server-side dedup only considers per-action tokens when present.

Key findings:
- Server dedup is per-action if explicit idempotency-token present; otherwise per-session only prevents exact-replay but not partial-ACK + resume replay scenarios.
- Client circuit-breaker replay can cause session-resume to replay a sequence where final ACKs were lost.

Suggested fix directions:
- Short-term: update SDK docs and examples to recommend per-action idempotency tokens for side-effectful tool calls.
- Mid-term: server to consider action-sequence checks for resumed sessions (compare KV cache offsets and known-acked indexes) and reject replays that would cause re-execution.
- Long-term: add explicit session resume handshake that returns a list of acknowledged action indices so clients can avoid replaying already-acked actions.

2026-03-10 12:45 - Customer (Elena Torres): SDKs: python 1.28.0, ts 0.34.1. We don't currently pass action-level idempotency keys; we rely on session scope. Circuit-breaker timeout 15s, immediate retry on close, no jitter.
2026-03-11 08:18 - Support (Maya Patel): Reproduced locally using customer's proxy and CB config — behavior reproduced. Escalating to SDK eng and SRE. Linking traces in ticket.

2026-03-12 09:05 - SRE (Priya Rao): Gateway trace shows partial ack followed by resumed connection. Gateway currently lacks a compact ack-map on session resume. Logged INT-4482 to track server-side handshake addition.

resolution:
Workaround provided: customer implemented per-action idempotency keys for critical tool calls and adjusted circuit-breaker to use exponential backoff with jitter. After the change, duplicate side-effects dropped to <0.01% in their test window.

Engineering follow-up:
- SDKs: land PRs to make per-action idempotency tokens easier to opt into and add guidance in quickstart (tracked in PRs).
- Server: INT-4482 created to implement session-resume ack-map and handshake; will evaluate approach and estimate in the next sprint.

Status: awaiting server-side change. Customer satisfied with workaround; ticket will remain open until INT-4482 has a planned ETA.
